source: AI fixer successful fixes without KB guidance

antiPatterns.why: Reduces readability, violates convention that fields are declared at top
Hard to find class constants when not grouped at top

correctPatterns.pattern: all fields at top of class

patterns.guidanceText: Move all field declarations to the start of the class, before any methods. Group static final constants first, then instance fields.
patterns.promptAdditions:
CRITICAL for FieldDeclarationsShouldBeAtStartOfClass:
- Move ALL field declarations to the top of the class body
- Order: static final constants, static fields, instance fields
- Place fields BEFORE any methods
- Keep field order consistent (public, protected, package, private)

antiPatterns.why: Ambiguous intent - unclear if default access was intentional or oversight

patterns.guidanceText: Add /* package */ comment before members with default (package-private) access to indicate the access level is intentional.
patterns.promptAdditions:
CRITICAL for CommentDefaultAccessModifier:
- Add /* package */ BEFORE the type declaration
- Format: /* package */ TypeName memberName;
- Apply to fields, methods, and nested classes with default access
- DO NOT change the access modifier, just add the comment

antiPatterns.why: While Java adds implicit super(), explicit call improves clarity

antiPatterns.pattern: exception constructor not passing message to parent

patterns.guidanceText: Add explicit super() or super(args) as the first statement in constructors. For exceptions, pass the message to the parent constructor.
patterns.promptAdditions:
CRITICAL for CallSuperInConstructor:
- Add super() or super(message) as FIRST statement in constructor
- For Exception subclasses, pass message to parent: super(message)
- If parent has only parameterized constructors, use appropriate super(args)
- super() must be the FIRST statement, before any other code

antiPatterns.pattern: single-letter variable names (i, j, k outside loops)

correctPatterns.pattern: i, j, k acceptable only in simple for loops

patterns.guidanceText: Rename short variables to descriptive names that explain their purpose. Exception: loop counters i, j, k in simple for loops.
patterns.promptAdditions:
CRITICAL for ShortVariable:
- Rename to describe PURPOSE not type (extensionIndex not intIndex)
- Common patterns:
  - 'i' for index → 'extensionIndex', 'startIndex', 'itemIndex'
  - 'f' for file → 'sourceFile', 'tempFile'
  - 'n' for count → 'itemCount', 'retryCount'
- Keep loop counters (i, j, k) in simple for loops
- Min 3 characters for variable names

antiPatterns.why: Redundant - Java provides implicit default constructor
Redundant - implicit super() is called automatically

correctPatterns.pattern: keep constructor if it has documentation

patterns.guidanceText: Remove empty default constructors as Java provides them implicitly. Keep only if there's documentation explaining why it's explicit.
patterns.promptAdditions:
CRITICAL for UnnecessaryConstructor:
- DELETE the empty constructor entirely, don't comment it out
- Exception: Keep if it has meaningful Javadoc
- Exception: Keep if required for framework (Spring, serialization)
- After removal, ensure no other code depends on explicit constructor
